react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary enrichment paradigms converge unambiguously on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 7.8e-13, fold-enrichment = 834) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 5.49e-06) both ranked KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top pathway, while mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its single highest-scoring pathway (p = 0.00025) with a remarkable 11/12 overlap. Five input metabolites map to this pathway across tools: L-tryptophan (C00078, the canonical entry substrate), serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) from the serotonin/melatonin branch, and quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) from the kynurenine degradation arm. The co-occurrence of both branches in a single differential set suggests the treatment perturbs the tryptophan node upstream, diverting flux simultaneously toward the biogenic-amines (serotonin–melatonin) and toward the neurotoxic kynurenine arm (quinolinic acid). The remaining three metabolites — O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346), 3-methyladenine (C00913), and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid (C01127) — appear as peripheral hits in mummichog (glycerophospholipid metabolism / purine metabolism), consistent with their chemical unrelatedness to the tryptophan core. RaMP additionally flagged WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR = 2.95e-11) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 3.96e-09), reinforcing that the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm is a major biological readout of the treatment effect. Cross-paradigm consensus is perfect: all three methods name tryptophan metabolism as #1, making it the sole high-confidence narrative driver.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on Tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-DB over-representation analysis (FDR 7.8e-13) identifies KEGG:map00380 as its top hit, with L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, quinolinic acid, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid forming a 5-metabolite input overlap against 54 reference compounds (fold-enrichment 834). MetaboAnalystR KEGG pathway-set enrichment independently returns hsa00380 (p-value 5.49e-06, rank 1), with four of those five metabolites confirmed by the same method. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis, operating on the empirical human metabolic network, reaches hsa00380 as its top-ranked pathway (p-value 8.4e-05) with 11 of 12 network members matched by the input set. The three serotonergic intermediates — L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin — additionally anchor the Reactome pathway Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (FDR 9.1e-09). Quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, the two kynurenine-branch metabolites, independently validate the NAD+ biosynthetic sub-pathway (WP:WP3645, FDR 9.6e-09). O-phosphoethanolamine is peripheral: it maps not to tryptophan metabolism but to glycerophospholipid and glycosphingolipid pathways via mummichog, reflecting its distinct metabolic origin (phosphatidylcholine head-group recycling). The convergence across ORA, PSEA, and m/z-network paradigms, supported by three distinct database namespaces (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome), constitutes a high-confidence biological finding: the treatment simultaneously up-regulates the biogenic-amine arm (tryptophan → serotonin → melatonin) and the neurotoxic kynurenine arm (tryptophan → kynurenine → quinolinic acid → NAD+).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary enrichment paradigms converge unambiguously on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 7.8e-13, fold-enrichment = 834) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 5.49e-06) both ranked KEGG:hsa00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top pathway, while mummichog m/z-direct analysis returned MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as its single highest-scoring pathway (p = 0.00025) with a remarkable 11/12 overlap. Five input metabolites map to this pathway across tools: L-tryptophan (C00078, the canonical entry substrate), serotonin (C00780) and melatonin (C01598) from the serotonin/melatonin branch, and quinolinic acid (C03722) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) from the kynurenine degradation arm. The co-occurrence of both branches in a single differential set suggests the treatment perturbs the tryptophan node upstream, diverting flux simultaneously toward the biogenic-amines (serotonin–melatonin) and toward the neurotoxic kynurenine arm (quinolinic acid). The remaining three metabolites — O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346), 3-methyladenine (C00913), and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid (C01127) — appear as peripheral hits in mummichog (glycerophospholipid metabolism / purine metabolism), consistent with their chemical unrelatedness to the tryptophan core. RaMP additionally flagged WP:WP4210 (Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production, FDR = 2.95e-11) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 3.96e-09), reinforcing that the kynurenine-to-NAD+ arm is a major biological readout of the treatment effect. Cross-paradigm consensus is perfect: all three methods name tryptophan metabolism as #1, making it the sole high-confidence narrative driver.
